healthcare system = the organised network of hospitals, clinics, staff and funding in a country
primary care = first-contact health services, especially GPs, dentists and pharmacies
secondary care = hospital and specialist services after a GP referral
paramedic = a trained emergency clinician who treats people at the scene and in an ambulance
midwife = a specialist who cares for women during pregnancy, birth and after
paediatrician = a doctor who specialises in the health of babies and children
anaesthetist = a doctor who gives anaesthetics and watches the patient during surgery
pharmacist = a professional who prepares and advises on medicines
telemedicine = medical consultation by phone or video instead of a face-to-face visit
walk-in centre = a clinic you can attend without booking in advance
out-of-hours service = medical help available when the usual GP surgery is closed
medical negligence = harm caused when care falls below the standard a patient should expect
mental health = the condition of your mind and emotions, including how you cope with life
anxiety disorder = a mental-health condition with intense, lasting worry that disrupts daily life
counselling = talking regularly with a trained person to work through emotional problems
stigma = unfair shame or discrimination attached to an illness or situation
depression = a mental illness with lasting low mood, loss of interest and often poor sleep
bipolar disorder = a condition with extreme swings between high and low mood
anorexia nervosa = an eating disorder involving severe food restriction and a distorted body image
post-traumatic stress disorder = a condition after a shocking event, with flashbacks, nightmares and high alertness
